chunks: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Obayd al-Dhabbi narrated to us, saying: I heard my father Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad saying: I heard my grandfather saying: I heard my father saying:

When Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Nishapur during the time of al-Ma'mun, I attended to his needs and managed his affairs as long as he was there. When he departed for Marv, I accompanied him to Sarakhs. When he left Sarakhs, I intended to accompany him to Marv, but after he had traveled one stage, he put his head out of the carriage and said to me: 'O Abu Abdullah! Return, may you be successful. You have performed what is incumbent upon you, and there is no limit to accompaniment.'

I said: 'By the right of al-Mustafa (the Prophet), al-Murtadha (Imam Ali), and al-Zahra (Fatima), tell me a hadith that will heal me so that I may return.' He said: 'You ask me for a hadith, and I have been removed from the neighborhood of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), not knowing what will become of my affairs.'
I said: 'By the right of al-Mustafa, al-Murtadha, and al-Zahra, tell me a hadith that will heal me so that I may return.'

He said: 'My father narrated to me from his grandfather that he heard his father saying: I heard my father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) saying that he heard the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Allah, the Exalted, said:'
'There is no god but Allah is My Name. Whoever says it sincerely from his heart will enter My Stronghold, and whoever enters My Stronghold is secure from My punishment.'
The author of this book (may God have mercy on him) said: 'This saying acts as a barrier for him from saying what Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden.'

key_terms.الزَّهْرَاءِ: Al-Zahra (The Shining One), a title for Fatima al-Zahra
key_terms.الْمُرْتَضَى: Al-Murtadha (The Pleased One), a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.الْمُصْطَفَى: Al-Mustafa (The Chosen One), a title for the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'sincerity' in the phrase 'There is no god but Allah is My Name' according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, highlights the humility of Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) during his transit from Nishapur to Marw, where he dismisses his servant after a brief journey to avoid excessive honor. The core teaching emphasizes the spiritual efficacy of the declaration 'La ilaha illa Allah' as a divine stronghold, with al-Saduq interpreting 'sincerity' (ikhlas) as adherence to divine commandments, thereby linking verbal affirmation with practical piety.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 39-2 Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Obayd al-Dhabbi narrated that he had heard that Abul Husayn ibn Ahmad quote on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of his father,

“When Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) entered Neishaboor at the time of Al-Ma’mun, I was at his service and took care of his needs as long as he was there until he departed towards Sarakhs. I accompanied him. I accompanied him when he wanted to leave Sarakhs to go to Marv. But as soon as we passed through one way-station, he brought out his head from his carriage andsaid, “O Aba Abdullah! Return. May you be successful. You have performed what is incumbent upon you. You need not accompany me anymore.” I said, “I swear by al-Mustafa (the Prophet), al-Mortadha (Imam Ali) and az-Zahra (Fatima). Please tell me one tradition to heal me so that I may return.”
He said, “Are you asking me for traditions? I have left the neighborhood of my grandfather - the Prophet of God (a.s.) - not knowing what will happen to my affairs.”
I said, “I swear by al-Mustafa, al-Mortadha and az-Zahra. Please tell me one tradition to heal me so that I may return.”

Then he said, “My father (a.s.) narrated that his father (a.s.) quoted on the authority of his father (a.s.) that he had heard his forefathers (a.s.) say that they heard their forefathers (a.s.) say that they heard Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) say that he had heard the Prophet (S) say that God - the Exalted the Magnificent - said,
There is no god but God is My Name. Whoever says it sincerely and whole-heartedly will enter My Stronghold. Whoever enters My Stronghold is secure from My punishment.”
The author of this book (a.s.heikh Sadooq) - may God forgive him - said, “Sincerity here means that these words should protect him from saying what God the Exalted the Honorable has forbidden.
